logic_errors: Step 4 sort key 1 ('Class. All pair rows before all single rows') enacts formulation 1 from the document's own falsification table ('Every pair above every single row - Lowered the score in 1,020 cases: an unrelated pair displaces a true single'; count reproduced exactly). The allele-sharing override only promotes a pair above singles SHARING an allele, so displacement of an unrelated true-allele single is unrepaired. Concrete synthetic counterexample: pool = Tier-B pair (chr2:3000 G>A + chr2:4000 T>C, both lanes) and Tier-A single (chr1:1000 A>G); truth = (chr1:1000 A>G, chr1:2000 C>T) with the partner allele excluded at Step 2 (representation). Step 4 order puts the Tier-B pair first: 25.0 rank points. Tier-first order: 50.0. The class key costs 25 points in a shape the rule itself can produce, contradicting the document's claim that its ordering claims were verified never to lower the score.

verify_rule.py R1 coverage gap: it enumerates permutations only for n in (2,3) while the gate accepts up to 10 rows (docs/22 Step 6) and the ladder has 10 rungs. At n=4 the same rule lowers the score in 5,220 of 327,600 comparisons. Mechanism: promote_allele_sharing inserts the pair at the single's position, shifting every row between them down one rank; at n<=3 a shift cannot cross a tier boundary (ranks 2,3 share the 50-point tier), at n>=4 it can (rank 3->4 crosses 50->25). First counterexample (reproduced verbatim): orig = [single chr1:1000, single chr1:2000, single chr2:3000, pair chr1:1000+chr1:2000], truth = (chr2:3000, chr2:4000): original scores 25.0 (partial at rank 3), ruled scores 12.5 (partial pushed to rank 4 by the insertion shift, though the pair shares no allele with it).

Pair-order preservation claim is false for the committed implementation and vacuously tested in-pipeline. (a) False in general: verify_rule.promote_allele_sharing([(chr2:3000,), (chr1:1000+chr1:2000), (chr2:3000+chr2:4000)]) returns [(chr2:3000+chr2:4000), (chr2:3000,), (chr1:1000+chr1:2000)] - the two pair rows swapped relative order, contradicting 'The relative order of two pair rows is never changed by this step'. (b) Vacuous in-pipeline: after the five-key sort, key 1 already places every pair above every single, so the promotion can never fire (0 of 3,000 random pools had a single above a pair post-sort; promotion changed the sorted order in 0 of 3,000). verify_determinism.py T4 therefore tests the constraint only in the regime where it is inert and proves nothing about the regime where it acts.

R2 overgeneralization: 'keeping the weaker one below never scored lower than dropping it' was measured only on 2-row files (ranks 1,2). With bystander rows it fails: keep = [pair chr1:1000+chr2:3000, single chr3:5000, single chr2:4000, pair chr1:1000+chr1:2000] scores 25.0 under truth (chr1:1000, chr1:2000) while dropping the last row scores 50.0. This is the document's own headline phenomenon (full match at rank 4 = 25 < partial at rank 1 = 50) re-entering through the 'both are kept' mandate for allele-sharing pairs; the R2 verification design cannot see it. The keep-policy may still be the right tradeoff under ignorance, but the stated measurement support is an unproven universal.
blocking_contract_issues: docs/22 Step 4 internally contradicts its own falsification table (logic error 1). A pre-registration whose stated value is that a reader can check the submitted file against a measurement-grounded rule cannot ship a primary sort key that the same document's measurement arm rejected. Either the class key must be demoted below tier (with the allele-sharing override retained as the only pairs-first mechanism, and the override fixed per logic error 2), or the falsification table's scope must be re-argued. Not fixable by re-running existing scripts; the ordering itself changes.

The verification scripts do not support the universal claims docs/22 makes at the row counts the gate allows (logic errors 2-4). Before any private run: verify_rule.py must enumerate n up to at least the shapes the rule can emit (cap 10) or the doc must state the verified bound; the promotion must be implemented as a stable partition that provably cannot shift unrelated rows across tier boundaries; T4 must be run on pre-sort orders where the promotion actually fires; R2 must be re-measured at rank-4 keeps or reworded as a tradeoff, not a domination claim.
suggestions: Ordinary definitional gaps (one-line fixes, no novel policy needed, but two operators could currently build different files): (1) 'the stricter lane's native output rank' is never defined - stricter by what measure, per allele or per gene, and what if the allele appears in only one lane; the synthetic verifier silently uses min(ranks) across lanes, which is one reading, not the stated one. (2) Missing native rank: pool alleles sourced from the candidate review dossier or region genotypes may have no lane rank at all; key 4 is undefined for them. (3) 'Rows appearing in both lanes' is undefined for pair rows, which are constructed artifacts - presumably 'both alleles appear in both lanes', but unstated; the verifier assigns the boolean randomly. (4) Step 2 quality exclusion vs Tier B overlap: an allele passing lane 1 but failing lane 2's recorded criteria is both 'dropped for quality' (its lane's criteria failed) and 'passing in one lane' (Tier B eligible) - which wins is unstated. (5) Alleles outside the nine audited regions have no reviewed quality record; whether no-record means keep or drop is unstated.

Duplicate allele across genes: if one (chrom,pos,ref,alt) is annotated to two genes, Step 4 forms pairs in both; the five-key order still resolves them (distinct allele sets cannot tie at key 5) and parse_submission's repeated-variant refusal is bypassed by --allow-repeated-pairings, which docs/22 rule 3 anticipates. No contradiction found; worth one sentence in the doc.

The doc's note that brute_force_hedging.py shows 48,252 for the equal-EPCR arm (either-metric union) is consistent with hedging_modes.py's separated 44,090 F-max / 7,216 rank-point counts (overlap 3,054); the table numbers are all reproduced by hedging_modes.py, which was re-run here.

Fix quality from the prior review that did land: the 75%/25% reclassification (36,456/12,152 reproduced), the five-key total order with executed totality and permutation-invariance (19,779 keys, 0 ties; 32,612 runs, 0 mismatches), the sensitivity-run and dossier disclosures, and the pinned exclusion sources. The determinism half of the September 19 fix is sound; the score-safety half is not.

summary: The September 19 measurement layer is genuine and reproduces exactly: all published counts (1,843,650 combos; 48,608 strict-below rank-point drops; 0 F-max drops; 44,090/7,216 equal-EPCR drops; 75.0%/25.0% wrong-partner/single reclassification; 1,020 formulation-1 falsifications; 19,779 keys with 0 ties; 32,612 permutations with 0 mismatches) re-ran to identical values against the pinned evaluator (SHA-256 prefix 6d18b581e65a45e1 verified), and the five ignored runtime scripts hashed identically before and after. The determinism fix (five-key total order) is real as executed. However, the September 19 fixes do NOT yet support a private shortlist run, for three reasons the prior review did not catch: (1) Step 4's class key ('all pair rows before all single rows') is literally the policy the document's own falsification table rejects ('Every pair above every single row ... 1,020 cases'), and the allele-sharing override cannot repair it because it does nothing for unrelated singles - demonstrated counterexample costs 25 rank points; (2) verify_rule.py tests only 2-3-row files while the gate cap is 10, and its R1 'never lowered the score' claim is false at n=4 (5,220 of 327,600 comparisons lowered, first counterexample reproduced verbatim); (3) the pair-order-preservation and keep-vs-drop claims are respectively falsified in general and overgeneralized. Determinism holds; score-safety of the actual Step 4 ordering does not.
